choices: 401 = missing/invalid credentials; 403 = authenticated but not authorised
questions.explanation: 401 is an identification failure; 403 is an authorisation failure.

questions.stem: Which CSS change skips layout and paint when the element is on a compositor layer?
questions.explanation: transform and opacity on a promoted layer go straight to the GPU compositor.

questions.stem: Which mitigation actually defends against SQL injection?
questions.explanation: Placeholders separate code from data. Escape lists are routinely bypassed.

questions.stem: fetch('/x') with a 404 response:
choices: Resolves with a Response whose ok is false
questions.explanation: fetch only rejects on network failure. Always check response.ok or status.

questions.stem: Which cookie flag prevents JS from reading the cookie?
questions.explanation: HttpOnly hides the cookie from document.cookie / DOM APIs.

questions.stem: Which is a sign of an N+1 query?
choices: One outer query plus one additional query per returned row, scaling with the result set
questions.explanation: Symptom: query count proportional to rendered list size. Fix with JOIN, IN batching, or populate.

questions.stem: In React, what does the dependency array `[]` mean for useEffect?
choices: Run once after first commit and clean up on unmount
questions.explanation: Empty deps means the effect doesn't depend on anything from render; it runs once.

questions.stem: Which event-loop order is correct in the browser?
questions.explanation: Run sync to completion, drain all microtasks, optionally render, then pick the next task.

questions.stem: PUT vs POST:
choices: PUT is unsafe, POST is safe
PUT is idempotent (replacing twice → same state); POST is not (creates twice)
questions.explanation: Idempotency is the key distinction. PUT puts the resource into a target state; POST appends.

questions.stem: Which is the right index for `WHERE country = ? AND age > ?`?
questions.explanation: Equality column first, range column after. The B-tree seeks then ranges.

questions.stem: SameSite=Lax cookie is sent on:
choices: Top-level cross-site navigations (e.g. clicking a link) but not on cross-site subresource requests/POSTs
questions.explanation: Lax is the modern default and blocks most CSRF on state-changing methods.

questions.stem: Predict: `[] + {}` evaluates to:
questions.explanation: Array toString gives ''; then '' + '[object Object]' = '[object Object]'.

questions.stem: Which is the safest place to display user-supplied bio in a page?
choices: Use textContent or a templating engine that auto-escapes
questions.explanation: textContent never parses HTML; templating engines (EJS, JSX) escape by default.

questions.stem: Which is true about React keys when rows can be reordered?
choices: Use a stable id from the data; index keys cause state to attach to the wrong row after reorders
questions.explanation: Stable, item-derived keys preserve component identity across reorders. Index keys silently misattribute state.

questions.stem: Which is the right authentication setup for a typical browser SPA?
choices: Short-lived access token + refresh token with refresh stored as HttpOnly Secure SameSite=Strict cookie
questions.explanation: Minimises both XSS exposure (refresh hidden from JS) and CSRF (SameSite=Strict).

questions.stem: Why is `setCount(c => c + 1); setCount(c => c + 1);` safer than `setCount(count + 1); setCount(count + 1);`?
choices: Functional updaters receive the latest queued value; positional updates may both capture the same stale count
questions.explanation: Two captured `count + 1` calls produce the same result; functional updaters compound correctly.

questions.stem: Best status code for a POST that violates a unique constraint?
questions.explanation: 409 Conflict signals a clash with existing resource state (e.g. duplicate email).

questions.stem: Which is correct about CSP?
choices: Content-Security-Policy restricts which scripts and resources can be loaded, blocking many XSS payloads
questions.explanation: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' blocks inline and cross-origin scripts, defusing most XSS vectors.

questions.stem: Which is the cleanest fix for layout thrashing?
choices: Batch DOM reads first, then perform all writes
questions.explanation: Avoid interleaving reads (which force layout) with writes (which invalidate it).

questions.stem: Which is the safest password storage?
choices: bcrypt/argon2 with appropriate cost and a per-password salt
questions.explanation: Password hashes must be slow on purpose; bcrypt/argon2 include cost factor and salt by design.

questions.stem: Which best describes IDOR?
choices: Direct object reference (often in URL or body) accepted without an authorisation check against the requester
questions.explanation: GET /api/orders/43 should verify the caller may view order 43, not assume the URL implies permission.

questions.stem: What does `aria-describedby` do?
choices: Links a control to an element whose contents the screen reader announces as additional description
questions.explanation: Used to attach help text or error messages to form controls.

questions.stem: Why does a typical industry recommendation favour 'start as a monolith'?
choices: A modular monolith avoids the operational tax of microservices until team/traffic scale justifies it
questions.explanation: Microservices solve organisational scaling more than technical scaling. Premature splitting compounds complexity.

questions.stem: Predict: `console.log(typeof null);`
questions.explanation: Famous JS quirk preserved for backward compatibility — typeof null is 'object'.

questions.stem: Which is the right pairing of OWASP topic to mitigation?
choices: XSS → escape output AND/or use a strict CSP
questions.explanation: Output-context-aware escaping + CSP is the real defense against XSS. The other three options are common but wrong answers.

questions.stem: What is the LCP target for a 'good' rating?
questions.explanation: Largest Contentful Paint: < 2.5s = good, 2.5-4s = needs improvement, > 4s = poor.

questions.stem: Which order is correct for the critical rendering path?
choices: Parse HTML+CSS → Render tree → Layout → Paint → Composite
questions.explanation: DOM + CSSOM combine into a render tree; layout computes geometry; paint fills pixels; compositor stitches layers.
